issue_context.title: Pods in Terminating status lasts much long time when subPath is set and contains a large number of directories
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

I ran a deployment with replicas 1 and use `subPathExpr` to set container's subpath dir, which uses NFS as the storage backend, and create about 100000 dirs in container's subPath dir,when delete the pod, it spent much more time to end `Terminating` status, and when the replicas increase to 10 and do the rolling update, at the same time dir nums in containers increase to 700000, it spent about 30 minutes to totally remove pod, which is intolerant.

### What did you expect to happen?

The pod is deleted fast.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Run a pod using subPathExpr as the volume mount.
2. Create 100000 dirs in the backend storage corresponds to the container volume mount
3. Delete the pod 
4. Inspect kubelet log：
We can find that it spent about 17s to clean the mount dir in kuelet.
```
I0118 15:28:47.192607    8551 subpath_linux.go:228] Cleaning up subpath mounts for /mnt/paas/kubernetes/kubelet/pods/c62a9d6e-8cba-44b9-b0c0-ee4d350b4f79/volume-subpaths/nfs-xxx

I0118 15:29:03.490373    8551 subpath_linux.go:313] Successfully cleaned subpath directory /mnt/paas/kubernetes/kubelet/pods/c62a9d6e-8cba-44b9-b0c0-ee4d350b4f79/volume-subpaths/nfs-xxx/test-nginx/0
```

I tried to fix this, and pr is here[#107669](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/107669)

review_comments: @msau42 do we only care about the files inside `/var/lib/kubelet/pods/<uid>/volume-subpaths/<volume>/<container name>/*` if so wouldn't `Readdir` work? I'm not sure why we need to to a traversal

Good question. I traced back to when we changed it from `Readdir` to `Walk` and found myself :-)

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/71804

The issue this was fixing was a subpath on an nfs server that became stale. What happened was that `Readdr` on a stale nfs mount would return an error, whereas `Walk` would pass through the error.

It may be worth adding a comment here explaining that for future readers. Also good to check if the e2e test added for the stale nfs issue is passing with this fix.

e2e test "Kubernetes e2e suite: [sig-storage] In-tree Volumes [Driver: nfs] [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] subPath should be able to unmount after the subpath directory is deleted [LinuxOnly]" passed
https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/107669/pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce-ubuntu-containerd/1484417919810015232/
Thanks for all your patience! I have added a detail comment trying to make it more clear.
